# Commands

This page is **generated** from the CLI itself — the `USAGE` help text in
`src/cli/main.ts`, cross-checked against the command dispatch in the same file.
Editing it by hand achieves nothing: the next `bun run docs:commands` overwrites
it, and CI fails when the committed copy does not match what the CLI offers. A
command that exists but is not in the help text, or is in the help text but does
not exist, fails the generator rather than producing a page that quietly lies.

It is the same text `parley --help` prints, so the two cannot disagree.

## Setting up and keeping current

### `parley update`

```
parley update [--check] [--yes]
```

replace this binary with the latest release

Flags: `--check`, `--yes`

### `parley buses`

```
parley buses
```

every bus on this machine, which one is busy, and where its panel is

### `parley adapters`

```
parley adapters
```

every project set up, and whether its skill is current with this binary

### `parley mcp`

```
parley mcp
```

run as an MCP server over stdio (for Codex, Kimi, Antigravity and anything else that speaks MCP)

### `parley init`

```
parley init --workspace
```

make this directory one bus for every repository inside it (VS Code multi-root workspaces)

Flags: `--workspace`

```
parley init [--yes] [--global]
```

install hooks and skill for detected harnesses. --global installs the Claude Code hooks once for every project — the only way every worktree is covered, since .claude/ is usually gitignored.

Flags: `--global`, `--yes`

### `parley uninit`

```
parley uninit
```

remove what init wrote

### `parley doctor`

```
parley doctor
```

diagnose transport, repo identity and the WSL boundary

### `parley status`

```
parley status
```

is a daemon up, and what does it hold

### `parley stop`

```
parley stop
```

shut the daemon down

## Talking

### `parley say`

```
parley say [--to NAME] [--priority high] "text"
```

Flags: `--priority`, `--to`

### `parley question`

```
parley question --to NAME "..." [--wait 60] [--ttl 600]
```

Flags: `--to`, `--ttl`, `--wait`

### `parley reply`

```
parley reply <id> "answer"
```

### `parley ack`

```
parley ack <id> ["got it, doing X"]
```

### `parley nudged`

```
parley nudged <id>
```

record that you woke them, so parley stops asking

### `parley questions`

```
parley questions
```

### `parley drain`

```
parley drain
```

### `parley history`

```
parley history [--limit 200]
```

Flags: `--limit`

## Territory

### `parley claim`

```
parley claim <paths...> [--intent "..."] [--auto]
```

Flags: `--auto`, `--intent`

### `parley release`

```

```

Flags: `--all`

## Watching

### `parley watch`

```
parley watch [--web] [--port N] [--detach] [--stop]
```

live panel: fronts, feed and pending requests. Opens watching; press i (or s on the web) to speak. --detach keeps the web panel up after you close the terminal; --stop shuts that one down. Each repository gets its own port, so panels for several projects run side by side.

Flags: `--detach`, `--port`, `--stop`, `--web`

## Permission

### `parley ask`

```

```

Flags: `--reason`, `--ttl`

### `parley requests`

```

```

### `parley deny`

## Knowledge that outlives the session

### `parley note`

```

```

Flags: `--body`, `--paths`, `--tags`, `--title`

### `parley decide`

```
parley decide --title "..." [--body "..."] [--paths a,b]
```

Flags: `--body`, `--paths`, `--title`

### `parley reverse`

```
parley reverse <id> [--reason "..."]
```

Flags: `--reason`

### `parley notes`

```
parley notes [--tag x] [--path p] [--kind decision] [--export] [--import] [--query "..." [--k N]]
```

Flags: `--export`, `--import`, `--k`, `--kind`, `--path`, `--query`, `--tag`

## Global flags

Every command takes these.

```
--json (machine output), --as NAME, --quiet
--help, --version
```
